chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: Brother Johnny Garland and day jobs versus music
summary: His brother Johnny played with no particular band and advised never letting music interfere with a job; a comparison with a blueprint man.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: I got a bad mouth. I got a fever blusht out of my mouth. You see, so I got a bad mouth. Now, what about your brother Johnny? Johnny Garland.

Who did he play with? Johnny didn't play with any particular person. When he was here. Because he said he never let music interfere with a job. He tried to teach me that. Always keep a job. It would depend on music. I couldn't see it that way. Oh, music. He was a blueprint. Which kind of? Blueprint. Oh, yeah. Like Louie Warnick.
Yeah, yeah. He was a blueprint man too. My brother's one.
For Dietzchen, I think. Is he living yet, Louie?
No, no. He's been there. No, I didn't. For Dietzchen, I think.
No, I didn't. He stayed around here in Wack. He used to play. Different people.
And he played a while with all of them.
